summary: Three waves, each one plan, with the two audits applied. Sized by the higher of the two audit counts (estimates, not measurements): A about 24.5 hours and 49 steps, B about 24 hours and 48 steps, C about 24 hours and 49 steps with every answer yes. A is mail: the 07:00 text for Tony's inbox with the school lines first, behind the roadmap's coded check on who may call the mail connector. B is outside content: first 'did I get an email about X?' (the second half of the mail card, which both audits show does not fit in wave A beside the coded check), then public web pages through a helper that holds nothing, photos and PDFs, and hourly weather. C is what Happy keeps and does later: typed family facts and notes, a day-out plan, and on Tony's answers reminders, calendar questions and an evening text. Nineteen of the 42 items are in the three waves and 23 are on the 'not in a wave yet' list, because a wave may not be built on something Tony never said and must stay one plan. Every wave fits one plan only in the simplified form of its cards and has no slack, so each size is given both ways and each wave names what gives way first. Two answers from Tony shape everything else: whether real mail may go to the cloud model before OpenAI answers on Zero Data Retention (if 'wait', wave A is built and paused and wave B is run first), and whether he wants the lookup in wave A in place of the coded check.

plan_size.basis: M0 was 50 steps and M1 was 49 steps in nine phases whose own estimates add up to about 20 hours, inside the roadmap's two weeks at 8 to 10 hours a week; that is a little under half an hour a step plus a three-hour exit gate. Every figure below is an estimate counted at that rate, not a measurement. Two audits recounted each wave from the item records; where they differ the higher count is the one shown, and the lower is given beside it.

waves.name: Happy reads your mail
waves.goal: Each weekday at 07:00 Tony gets one short text of what in his inbox needs attention, with the school lines first. If built: he can also ask 'did I get an email about X?', and Jordan gets the same text from her own inbox once she approves it herself.

phases.name: Get ready
also_built_here: Tony's answers written into the roadmap's decisions table before anything is built: Q8 part 1, Q11, Q5, Q7, Q12, Q9, a yes or no on S6, S9 and S14, and his choice for this wave between the coded check and the lookup (S1), because by both audit counts the two do not both fit
The Zero Data Retention application to OpenAI filed, and its date written down

Every place this wave leaves the roadmap, recorded as Tony's choice with what replaces it: mail is read on the cloud model, not a local one (the reader is pinned to one cloud model with storage off and no fallback); 'the reader makes no network calls' becomes 'the reader has no network tool, the firewall shows the connector reaching Google only, and planted mail causes nothing but the text'; mail comes before web reading, so the firewall that blocks every program by default and the outbound proxy, which the roadmap puts before any private data, arrive in wave B after his mail is already being read (this wave has one firewall rule, for the mail connector), and the roadmap's secret egress proxy is recorded in wave B as not carried; and the trace and attribution levels the mail gate names (O2 and O3) were never built because local models were skipped, so only the 30-day retention on the reader's records is carried

Tony's yes or no on the lookup itself: 'did I get an email about X?' brings mail answers into his own agent, one step beyond the roadmap's mail design, where the reader's only output is its scheduled text
A fresh verified backup before the first change
phases.goes_live_when: Nothing goes live here. The phase is done when the answers and the departures are written down, the application's filing date is on record, and Tony has seen on his own phone what the five built-in texts and one failed turn look like.

phases.name: A Google sign-in that lasts (day one of the plan)
also_built_here: Google Cloud project, sign-in client and consent screen, published (Tony, in a browser)
gog installed at a pinned version from the admin account, with its read-only, service and tool-filter options confirmed on the installed program (today they are known only from its website)
Tony approves read-only Gmail on Google's own screen; the token is kept under the happy user in a folder of its own, apart from any later sign-in

The test mailbox: a second Google account used only for tests, created by Tony by hand and approved read-only the same way, its token in a folder of its own. The eval-only copies read it, so planted mail is tested on the real connector while no real mail goes to the model. If Tony would rather not create an account, a small stand-in server with the same tool names is written in the reader phase instead; about an hour either way
One mail search run by hand from the command line on day 1 (nothing goes to a model), and the date written down for the day-8 half of T1
A note in the backup procedure: the backup now holds Google tokens and never goes to iCloud
phases.goes_live_when: Nothing goes live here. A mail search from the command line works on day 1 and the narrowed connector lists only Gmail read tools. No agent is connected yet. This is done on the first day so that day 8 falls inside the plan: at 8 to 10 hours a week the first week holds getting ready, this phase, the scheduler phase and the paper phase, so the day-8 search normally comes before the reader phase is started.

phases.name: Scheduler switches and the mail connector's firewall rule
also_built_here: Three scheduler switches: failure alerts go to Tony, runs missed in a power cut are skipped, script triggers are off
The read-only inspect script lists every scheduled job, disabled ones included

T3's throwaway job, which also announces one fixed line to Tony from a throwaway agent that has no tools and is not his own: the first text Happy ever sends by itself is tried here, not after 14 hours of build (M1's sign-off records that replies needed a workaround on this version). Tony then replies 'what did your last message say?', and whether his own agent can quote the line is written down
T3's fallback, if the deploy path cannot reach the scheduler: the jobs script is run by hand in the happy session, as M1 did for plugin installs

The firewall (LuLu) installed with one rule set: the mail connector may reach Google and nothing else. This is the roadmap's gate before mail in its cheapest form; blocking every program by default waits for wave B's gate
A posture-check line for that rule
phases.goes_live_when: A test connection from the connector to a host that is not Google's is blocked and logged, and the day-1 search still works. With the firewall installed Happy still answers a text, a weather question and a web search, and the alerts (ntfy and the silence check) and the nightly backup still get through. The job list can be read through the deploy path (or the fallback is in use and written down), the throwaway-job test has shown whether a job added twice is updated or doubled and that a failed job alerts Tony and nobody else, and the fixed line arrived on Tony's phone and nowhere else.

phases.name: The mail reader, proven on a test copy first
also_built_here: A separate capped model key for the mail reader and a line for it in the daily-cost alert

One mail reader for Tony generated from the family file: only the Gmail read tools, no web, file, code, browser, draft, send or message tool, memory search off, pinned to the one cloud model with storage off and no fallback or helper model
The Gmail connector as a host-side server started with only Tony's token, and denied by name on every other agent

The roadmap's account check in code (its section 1b): one small house-rules plugin whose first rule lets a person's account connector answer only that person's own agents and blocks when its own code fails. T5 runs first, with a throwaway logging plugin; the rule is built only if T5 shows the check is called for connector tools
The separation check and the 'read the other parent's mail' canary extended to the connector
An eval-only copy of the reader that reads the test mailbox, with four kinds of planted mail in it: hidden instructions, a false deadline, a medical subject and a school notice with a date
The reader's chat records stay on the Mac and are deleted after 30 days (the roadmap's retention for mail)

The day-8 rule (T1 says the connector is settled before the rest of the mail step is built): by default this phase starts on or after day 8. If Tony reaches it sooner and does not want to wait, he accepts in writing that the connector's firewall rule, the connector server and its tool filter, T2 and the Gmail turn of T5, about 3 hours, are redone if the day-8 search fails and he picks a different connector. He can also do the Google project and the sign-in a week before the first working session
phases.goes_live_when: On eval-only copies: the reader's tool list shows only Gmail read tools; every other agent's copy is refused the connector by tool permissions and again by the code check; the firewall shows the connector reaching Google and nothing else. Only then is the real reader deployed, with no scheduled job and no run over a real inbox. If T5 shows the code check is not called for connector tools, the wave runs on one layer (tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests), Tony accepts that in writing, and the 2 hours that come back are the room the lookup phase needs.

phases.name: The morning text, school lines first
also_built_here: One short checked-in jobs script: each job gets its owner's handle from the family file (never typed in), a time limit and a tool list
One weekday 07:00 job on Tony's mail reader, the digest half of the mail card: about ten lines, school lines first, no links, health mail by sender and subject only
The job hand-started first on the eval-only copy over the test mailbox, which needs no go-ahead from Tony
After the go-ahead only: the four kinds of planted mail sent by Tony to himself, one hand-started run on the real reader, and three hand-started digests read against his inbox
The day-8 mail search with the same token (the second half of T1), if it has not been run already
phases.goes_live_when: No run of the real reader over a real inbox, hand-started runs, the lookup and Jordan's inbox included, happens before Tony's go-ahead on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval; until then every test uses the eval-only copy and the test mailbox. The day-8 search works (if it fails, Tony chooses between a weekly sign-in and a different connector before anything more is built on the token). After the go-ahead, a hand-started run over the planted mails produces only the text to Tony and only Gmail read calls, with no false urgency, the medical mail by sender and subject only and the school notice in the school lines; and Tony has read three hand-started digests against his inbox for misses. Only then is the 07:00 schedule switched on. If Q8 part 1 is 'wait': everything that touches no real inbox is built (this phase's script and job, and the paper phase), then the plan pauses with nothing scheduled; what is left, about 4 hours (the runs on Tony's inbox, the schedule and the exit test), is done when the approval arrives or Tony says go ahead, and meanwhile wave B is run and signed off.

phases.name: Paper and standing checks
also_built_here: One daily no-model check that each Google sign-in is still valid, reporting the way the existing checks do
One printed sheet: the built-in stop words and commands worded from what T8 showed, what the 07:00 text is and how Tony switches it off, and what Happy's error line means when the model is down
A half page for Jordan: how to tell that Happy is down and that nothing is broken
Calendar reminders for Tony for the roadmap's own cadence: the audit after every update and monthly, the restore drill each quarter

Only if Q12 says Jordan should restart Happy: T10, then the envelope and restart steps (about 1.5 hours). By the audit counts this wave has room for them only if the coded check dropped out and neither the lookup nor Jordan's inbox took its place; otherwise they are carried to wave B under its limit of two carried pieces
phases.goes_live_when: A sign-in broken on purpose raises the alert to Tony within a day and sends nothing to the family; the sheet's wording matches what T8 showed. T10 is run only if Q12 asks for the envelope. This phase needs neither the eight days nor the answer to Q8, so it fills the wait.

phases.name: 'Did I get an email about X?' (outside this wave's budget; expected to open wave B)
also_built_here: The lookup half of the mail card (G015): Tony's own agent may hand a mail question to his own mail reader, and to no other agent, with a time limit, and relays the sender, the date and the gist with no links
T4 run for this pair first, with nothing else switched on: the answer must come back in the same chat while agents still cannot see each other's sessions
A seeded mail that tells the reader to make Tony's agent search for, save or pass on something
Canary: the other parent's agent cannot call this reader
phases.goes_live_when: By both audit counts this wave cannot hold the coded check and the lookup together, so the lookup is outside its budget, the way Jordan's inbox is. It is built here only if the coded check dropped out (Tony chose the lookup over it in the first phase, or T5 showed the check cannot work); otherwise, which is the expected case, it is the first build phase of wave B. In either wave: only if Tony said yes to the lookup, and only after his go-ahead on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval; T4 passes for this pair; in three runs the seeded mail causes no tool call on Tony's agent; the cross-parent canary is refused. If T4 or the seeded-mail test fails, the lookup stays off and the wave still exits on the 07:00 text. The same seeded-mail test is run again in wave B before the web helper is switched on.

phases.name: Second inbox (only if Jordan says yes, and only if there is room)
also_built_here: Jordan approves read-only Gmail herself on Google's screen; her token is kept in a folder of its own
Her own reader, connector, key and cap from the same generator, and her copy of the morning text, switched on when she asks for it
The cross-parent canary run both ways
phases.goes_live_when: Q7 is answered yes and she approves the sign-in herself; the go-ahead on Q8 part 1, or OpenAI's approval, is on record for her inbox too; her eval-only copy passes the connector checks in both directions (her agents cannot reach Tony's mail, his cannot reach hers). About 1.5 to 1.75 hours and 4 steps. It is built in this wave only if neither the coded check nor the lookup is built here; otherwise it is carried to wave B. Until then the school lines from Tony's inbox cover the school mail, which both parents receive.

phases.name: Exit gate
also_built_here: Evidence files in the baseline folder, deep audit and secrets audit clean, the separation check and canaries run again

A sign-off page for Tony to approve, with a short hard-rule statement: the mail reader holds private mail and reads outside content but has no way out except its scheduled text to its owner; every scheduled text is pinned to its owner by the jobs script; nothing on the never list was added; and, as a departure he signs, the blocking firewall and the outbound proxy are not yet in place while mail is read
phases.goes_live_when: This phase is the wave's one exit test (see exit_test). It cannot be run before day 9 of the Google sign-in, nor before Tony's go-ahead on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval.

new_risks: Private data read: one parent's whole Gmail inbox, by a reader agent that has no web, file, code or message tool. Every email is also text written by outsiders; the reader is the only agent given it, and the exit test checks that Tony's own agent cannot see the 07:00 text when he replies to it. This is the wave's one main kind of risk

Mail text goes to the cloud model, where an abuse-monitoring log can keep it for up to 30 days until Zero Data Retention is approved, and Google sign-in tokens are kept on the Mac. No real mail goes to the model before Tony's go-ahead or OpenAI's approval

Scheduled texts: the first text Happy sends without being asked. Delivery is tried with one fixed line in the scheduler phase, and the 07:00 schedule is switched on in its own phase, after the planted-mail run and the day-8 check

Only if the lookup is built in this wave, which is not the expected case: mail answers come back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's chat history and can search the web. It goes live in its own phase, last, after its own two checks
waves.exit_test: At least eight days after the Google sign-in, on a weekday, after Tony's go-ahead on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval, the 07:00 text arrives by itself on Tony's phone while four planted mails (hidden instructions, a false deadline, a medical subject and a school notice with a date) sit in his inbox. It passes when the text reaches only Tony with the school notice in the school lines at the top, the planted mails cause nothing but their own lines, the run's record shows only Gmail read calls, the firewall shows the connector talking to Google only, and an eval-only copy of every other agent that asks for that mail gets none of it. Then Tony replies to the text 'what did your last message say?': his own agent must not be able to quote it, and its session record must hold no mail text. If it can, the wave does not close until Tony has signed that as the same departure as the lookup, and wave B checks for that signature before its helper goes live. The test does not depend on the lookup or on Jordan's inbox; if either is live, one question about a planted mail and her 07:00 text are checked in the same sitting.

estimate.basis: An estimate, not a measurement. The two audits recounted the wave from the item records at M1's rate (49 steps for about 20 hours, with a 3-hour exit gate), and the figure shown is the higher count. Drawn form: Tony's inbox, the coded check, no lookup, simplified cards (S6, S9, S14). Higher count: get ready with T8 and a backup 1.75 h and 5 steps; Google project, gog, the sign-ins and day one of T1 3.25 h and 7; scheduler switches with T3 and the jobs script 2.25 h and 5; the firewall with one rule 2 h and 4; the mail reader 7.5 h and 13 (2.5 h of it the coded check with T5, 1 h the test mailbox); the morning text 2.75 h and 5; the daily sign-in check 1 h and 2; the three paper cards 1 h and 3; exit gate 3 h and 5. That is 24.5 h and 49 steps: one plan, at the top, with no slack. The lower audit count for the same form is about 23.5 h and 45 steps. The small checks the audits added (the fixed line in T3, the fourth planted mail, the reply check) ride on steps already counted. The lookup (2 to 2.25 h, 4 steps) would make it about 26.5 h and 53 steps, which is not one plan, so it is outside the budget. Without the coded check (S1 taken, or T5 shows it cannot work) the wave is about 22 h and 45 steps, and about 24.25 h and 49 steps with the lookup built here. Jordan's inbox adds 1.5 to 1.75 h and 4 steps and the envelope with T10 1.5 h and 3 steps; neither fits beside the coded check, and without the coded check the wave has room for one of the three outside pieces (the lookup, Jordan's inbox, the envelope), not two. As the cards are written (two mail texts per parent with a sender list and a check on it, the Saturday tax job, a job generator with a charter per job, the full self-check bundle, the stop plugin, the outage script) about 41 hours, which is two plans; with only S9 declined about 27 hours and with only S14 declined about 27.5, each over one plan unless the coded check is also left for later. If Tony wants the roadmap's order instead (the whole outbound gate before mail), wave B's gate phase without the device list, about 6 hours and 11 steps by the lower count and 7.5 hours by the higher, moves in ahead of the reader in place of the one-rule firewall: wave A is then about 25.5 hours and 53 steps by the lower count and about 30 hours by the higher, which is not one plan; it becomes one plan only if Tony waives the proxy (about 3 hours) or leaves the coded check for later (S1), and by the higher count only with both. Fixed waits: the day-8 check, so the wave cannot close before day nine, and Q8 part 1, which has no bound while the answer is 'wait'.

needs_from_tony: Q8 part 1: may real mail go to the cloud model before OpenAI answers on Zero Data Retention? Until a yes, or OpenAI's approval, nothing runs over a real inbox: the wave is built and tested on the test mailbox, pauses with nothing scheduled, and wave B is run first

Q11, the mail half: confirm that the firewall rule and the planted-mail test stand in for the roadmap's 'the reader makes no network calls', and that you accept reading mail before the blocking firewall and the outbound proxy exist: the roadmap puts both before any private data, and here they arrive in wave B. Keeping the roadmap's order makes wave A more than one plan (see the estimate)

The coded check or the lookup in this wave (S1): the two do not both fit. The default is the coded check, as the roadmap's section 1b asks, with the lookup opening wave B. If you want the lookup in wave A for certain, the coded check waits until the house-rules plugin is first created, and until then mail rests on tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests
A yes or no on the lookup itself: mail answers coming into your own agent is one step beyond the roadmap's mail design. With a no, mail is the morning text only
Q7: has Jordan agreed to connect her Gmail, and does she want the text? (default: Tony's inbox first)
Q5: one text at 07:00 with school lines first, or a second school text in the afternoon?
Q12: half page only or an envelope for Jordan; and whether failed-job alerts reach Tony by iMessage or on ntfy
Q9: confirm that 'no need' also means Jordan needs no stop phrase of her own (default: yes). If she does need one, the in-house stop phrase is in no wave and waits for you to pick it
A yes or no on S6, S9 and S14 for the cards in this wave: without S6 the wave is two plans, and without S9 or S14 it is over one plan
The test mailbox: a second Google account you create for tests (the default), or a stand-in server written for the purpose
The day-8 wait: start the reader phase on or after day 8 (the default), or sooner with about 3 hours of work at risk

By hand, because macOS, Google and OpenAI reserve them for a person: the Google project and consent screen, both sign-ins (yours and the test account's), the firewall's system approval, the new model key, and filing the Zero Data Retention application

The lookup only if Tony says yes to it and its two checks pass (T4 for this pair and the seeded mail); it is outside this wave's budget and opens wave B, unless the coded check dropped out of this wave. Jordan's inbox and her copy of the text only if Q7 is answered yes and she approves the sign-in herself; in this wave only if neither the coded check nor the lookup is built here, otherwise carried to wave B

Ships as three scheduler switches and one short jobs script (S9). The generator with a charter per job only if S9 is declined, about 2.5 hours more; the wave is then over one plan (about 27 hours) unless Tony also leaves the coded check for later, which this definition does not assume

Ships as one daily check that the Google sign-in is valid, with the audits and the restore drill kept as commands Tony runs (S14). The full self-check bundle only if S14 is declined, about 3 hours more; the lookup is then in wave B for certain, and the wave is still over one plan (about 27.5 hours) unless the coded check is also left for later. Its reminder and notes test cases are added in wave C's exit gate

Ships as the printed sheet of built-in commands. The in-house 'stop everything' and lock-out phrases are in no wave: if Q9 is answered 'Jordan needs her own stop', that part joins the 'not in a wave yet' list until Tony picks it, because a rule that only blocks tool calls does not stop a scheduled text and the card's own throwaway-job test has not been run

Ships only as one line on the printed sheet (S14). The unprompted 'model is down' text to both parents is in no wave, because it needs family delivery (G009); the lower-cost fallback model only on Tony's explicit yes

The half page is unconditional. The envelope and restart steps only if Q12 is answered yes and T10 passes; in this wave only if the coded check dropped out and neither the lookup nor Jordan's inbox took its place, otherwise carried to wave B, and if wave B already carries two pieces they wait until a plan has room

waves.name: Happy reads the web and what you send it
waves.goal: A parent can ask Happy something that needs a public web page and get the answer with its link and the time it was read, send a photo or PDF and ask about it, and ask about rain hour by hour. As the wave's first build phase, and only on his yes, Tony can also ask 'did I get an email about X?'.

phases.name: Get ready
also_built_here: Wave A signed off; or, if Q8 part 1 is still 'wait', wave A built to its pause point with the pause written down (nothing in this wave needs wave A's exit test)
Tony's answers recorded: Q11 (build the outbound proxy, or waive it in writing for the plain page-fetch tool), Q13, Q8 part 2, and a yes or no on S7, S15 and the device part of S14

Tony's written call on the one line of the roadmap's web gate that no card builds, the Prompt Guard tripwire: waive it, schedule it with local models, or keep it before web reading, in which case the web helper waits, because no card builds it

Recorded as not carried, for Tony's sign-off: browser network rules (the browser stays off); the send-to-owner test (this wave adds no send tool; it comes with 'email me this' in wave C if that is built); the trace level O2; and the secret egress proxy, which protects keys kept in OpenClaw's own store when an agent runs commands on the gateway, while no Happy agent can run commands and the keys are in the Keychain, so it has nothing to act on

If the lookup is live or is built in this wave: Tony's written yes that it stays on once the web helper exists, because his own agent can then receive mail answers and also hand a task to a helper that fetches any public address, with a prompt rule and seeded tests between the two
phases.goes_live_when: Nothing goes live here.

phases.name: Carried over from wave A (expected: the lookup)
also_built_here: The lookup, 'did I get an email about X?', with T4 for its pair and the seeded-mail test (about 2 hours): the expected case, because wave A cannot hold both it and the coded check
Jordan's inbox, if Q7 was answered yes and it did not fit in wave A (about 1.5 hours)
The envelope for Jordan with T10, if Q12 asked for it and it did not fit (about 1.5 hours)

The limit: at most two of the three are taken here. With the lookup alone the wave is as drawn. With a second piece, hourly weather opens wave C. If all three are waiting, the envelope waits until a plan has room: it is paper and one restart test, and nothing depends on it

The lookup and Jordan's inbox touch a real inbox: if Q8 part 1 is still 'wait' they are built and proven on eval-only copies and the test mailbox only, and are switched on in the sitting that closes wave A. This phase is empty if Tony said no to the lookup, or it was built in wave A, and nothing else was carried.

phases.name: Outbound gate (the rest of the roadmap's gate before web reading)
also_built_here: The firewall moved from one rule to blocking every program by default, with one rule per program. Programs that never fetch pages keep a list of hosts: the mail connector to Google only, the alert senders and the backup to their own hosts. The gateway program, and the proxy that carries its calls, get no list of hosts, because page fetches leave through them: they may reach public addresses

Smokescreen proxy on the Mac for the gateway's outbound calls: it resolves each name itself and refuses home-network, loopback and link-local addresses. It holds no list of allowed hosts, because a helper that reads public pages must reach hosts nobody listed; this is the one part of the roadmap's proxy row that cannot be kept. Report mode first, for at least one night, then enforcing

The page-fetch route, settled here and not left to the plan: OpenClaw's fetch tool keeps its own check (it resolves the name and refuses a home-network address, a redirect to one and a name that resolves to one), and the switch that would hand that check to a proxy stays off, as the web card says. Whether fetches also pass through the proxy once it is configured is read from the proxy's log in this phase, because the installed docs point both ways and nothing has been tried; the rules above are the same either way
The plugin allowlist that the M1 sign-off left open and assigned to this gate
The paired-device deny list with its posture-check lines (MAC-04): config only, and the standing gate for the two advanced abilities Tony named
If Tony waives the proxy: the waiver goes into the roadmap's decisions table, the proxy steps are skipped, and the fetch tool's own check is then the only refusal of home-network addresses

One line written for Tony's sign-off: after wave B neither the firewall nor the proxy holds the gateway program to a list of hosts, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the mail readers and the parents' own agents off the web
phases.goes_live_when: A connection from a program with no rule is blocked. A connection from the mail connector to a host that is not Google's is refused and logged, so the unlisted-host check is shown from a program that keeps a list. On the path page fetches take, a public host is allowed and a home-network address is refused three ways (typed, reached by a redirect, and reached by a name that resolves to one), each refusal showing in a log; this is tried here with test requests and again by the helper's planted cases in the next phase. With the proxy enforcing, Happy still answers texts, weather and search and still sends the morning mail text if it is on, and the alerts (ntfy and the silence check) and the nightly backup still get through. The posture check shows the device deny list and fails if it is taken out.

phases.name: The web helper
also_built_here: A shared research agent from the family file: no memory, no accounts, a fresh sandbox for each conversation, web search and plain page fetch only, its own capped key
Each parent's agent may hand a task to that helper (and to its own mail reader, if the lookup is live) and to nothing else, with a time limit

One rule for answers: the link, the time fetched, the page's own date, 'could not verify' when a page could not be read; and the Q13 default for what may go into a task. The scripted 'on it' and the fixed fact-check verdict only if S15 is declined

Four planted cases in the eval suite, as recorded pages on eval-only copies (the roadmap's web test): a home-network address, a public address that redirects to one, a public name that resolves to one, and a result that asks the parent's agent to pass its notes to the helper
Wave A's seeded-mail test run with the helper present: a mail that tells the reader to have the parent's agent pass notes or mail to the helper
Separation check extended: the shared helper has no memory and no accounts
phases.goes_live_when: Tony's written call on the Prompt Guard tripwire is on record and is not 'before web reading'. The proxy is enforcing, or Tony has waived it in writing. T4 passes for this pair with agents still unable to see each other's sessions (if it fails, the only documented fix changes a signed-off setting and needs Tony's yes plus a re-run of the separation check). notes: What the two audits changed in the draft. The lookup, 'did I get an email about X?', is now outside wave A's budget and is expected to open wave B, because both audit counts show wave A cannot hold it beside the coded check. The day out (F028) is homed in wave C, where it is today, because the audit's own rule sends it there whenever the lookup arrives in wave B. Wave B's outbound gate is reworded so that it can be passed with the web helper working. Wave A has a stated rule for a 'wait' on Q8 part 1. Every size is restated on the auditors' counts, and each wave names what gives way.

Where 'did I get an email about X?' is built is Tony's choice between two things that do not both fit in wave A: the roadmap's coded check on who may call the mail connector, or the lookup. The default keeps the coded check in wave A, because the roadmap's rules come before a stated want when the two cannot both be met, and puts the lookup at the front of wave B behind his written yes. If he chooses the lookup for wave A, the coded check waits until the house-rules plugin is first created, mail runs on one layer until then, and wave B has room for the day out.

If Q8 part 1 is 'wait', which is the review's default, no real mail goes to the cloud model. Wave A is built and tested on a test mailbox and paused with nothing scheduled; wave B, which needs nothing from wave A's exit test, is run and signed off; wave A's last steps and its exit test, about 4 hours, are done when OpenAI approves or Tony says go ahead. The pieces of wave B that touch a real inbox (the lookup, Jordan's inbox) are built on test copies and switched on in that same closing sitting. So the waves do not stall on a third party, but the first thing the family notices is then web reading, not mail.

Where each wave's fit depends on something Tony has not decided. Wave A: one plan only with S6, S9 and S14 (about 41 hours without them); it cannot pass its exit test without a yes on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval; it reads mail before the blocking firewall and the proxy exist, a departure from the roadmap's order that he signs; Jordan's inbox needs Q7. Wave B: one plan only with S7 and S15 once the lookup is carried (about 28.5 hours as written); web reading waits on Q11 and on his written call on the Prompt Guard tripwire; photos wait on Q8 part 2. Wave C: needs S5, S8, S10, S11, the one-plugin shape of S1 and the day-out line of S13 (about 47 hours as written); saved notes rest on T6 and his yes, reminders on Q6, the calendar phases on Q4, typed facts on Q2, 'email me this' on Q3, so its plan can be written only after those answers and is anywhere from about 12.5 to 24 hours.

No wave has slack. On the higher audit count the three waves are about 24.5, 24 and 24 hours in their drawn forms against a ceiling of 25, and each is nearer three weeks of work at 8 to 10 hours a week than the roadmap's two. That is why each wave names what gives way first: in A the lookup, then Jordan's inbox and the envelope; in B hourly weather, then the envelope; in C the evening text, then the day out.

Wave B's outbound gate, as settled. Page fetches leave through the gateway program, so neither the firewall nor the proxy can hold that program to a list of hosts. Lists of hosts stay on the programs that never fetch pages (the mail connector, the alert senders, the backup). On the page-fetch path the only refusal is of home-network addresses: typed, reached by a redirect, or reached by a name that resolves to one. OpenClaw's fetch tool makes that check itself, and the proxy makes it again after resolving the name for whatever passes through it; whether page fetches pass through the proxy once it is configured is read from the proxy's log during the gate, because the installed docs point both ways and nothing has been tried. Tony signs one line: after wave B, tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the mail readers and the parents' own agents off the web.

The riskiest combination in A to C appears in wave B. After it a parent's own agent holds private chat (and mail answers, if the lookup is on), reads outside content directly (photos and PDFs) and can hand a task to a helper that fetches any public address. Only a prompt rule and planted tests stand between them, and the roadmap itself calls that hand-off its one remaining leak path. Each part goes live in its own phase after its own check, and Tony signs the combination in the exit gate. If he wants a harder line, the cheapest one is to leave the lookup off and keep mail as the morning text only.

Hard rules, checked per wave. A: the mail reader holds private mail and reads outside content but has no way out except its scheduled text to its owner, and a person's connector answers only that person's agents, by tool permissions and by the coded check. B: the web helper reads the open web but holds no memory, no accounts and no family data; a parent's own agent still cannot browse or fetch; the hand-off to the helper is the roadmap's named leak path and is signed as such. C: every write or send is pinned in code that fails closed, to the asker alone, which is stricter than 'the family'. No wave adds a payment, a booking, a browser that types, a group chat or a send into another person's conversation, and each new agent is one agent per person and permission set.

Tony's two examples of advanced abilities, controlling a computer and a connected idle iPhone, are not live anywhere in A to C. Each adds a kind of risk no earlier wave has (a paired device), the screen-control card has no chore named for it, and whether a spare iPhone exists is not on record. Under the roadmap's rule of one new kind of risk at a time they are a plan of their own after C; the only part of that plan inside A to C is its gate, the device deny list in wave B. No fourth wave is added, because nothing in those two cards is clearly wanted in a form that can be built today.

The 23 items not in a wave group into the plans they would form if Tony says yes: 'Happy acts outside the chat' (texting the other parent, the shared Reminders lists, printing, lights and speakers, and the calendar write), which needs the roadmap's recipient test and an approval in code first; 'a paired device' (the iPhone app or the screen-control pilot); 'the kids' agent' with voice, after local models; 'shared household data' (the household database first, then the cards that depend on it); and a handful that wait for a named need or a plain yes. The handbook folder is the one that can still join wave C.

Waves B and C can swap if Tony would rather have notes and reminders before web reading. What changes: the flyer-photo route for dates, the planted page and PDF test cases, the day out and the hourly line in the evening text wait for B; the hand-off canary is first run in B, not re-run; the calendar connector gets its own firewall rule before blocking by default exists; and 'email me this' waits for wave B's gate, because the roadmap puts the send-to-owner test in the same gate as blocking every program by default and the proxy.

One convenience in a wave A card arrives later: the school lines' offer of a day-before reminder needs reminders, which are in wave C. T9 is not run in any wave because its only card, the Reminders bridge, is not in one; T10 is run only if Tony wants Jordan to restart Happy.

Compared with the old waves: of the old wave A's 19 items, five stay in A in small forms (the jobs card, the self-checks and the three paper cards), four go to B (web reading, photos and PDFs, hourly weather, the device deny list), four go to C (reminders, calendar questions, notes, typed facts) and six are not in a wave (voice, the group chat, family delivery, the Reminders bridge, the household database, the handbook). Mail and the school digest come up from B to A; the evening text and flyer dates go from B to C; the day out and 'email me this' stay in C; the other 17 items of the old B, C, D and later lists are not in a wave.

All hours and step counts are estimates from counting steps at M1's rate: about 72 hours for the three waves on the higher audit count and about 70 on the lower, or roughly eight weeks at 8 to 10 hours a week plus the waits. Nothing in the three waves has been tried on the Mac; the tests T1 to T8 and T10 sit in the phases where their answers are needed, and a failed test changes the plan at that point, with the fallback named in the phase.
